Madagascar Mining Sector Posts Steady Growth as Nickel, Cobalt Output Rises

ANTANANARIVO, Madagascar, June 20—Madagascar’s metals and mining industry reported steady growth in the first quarter of 2024, driven by higher production volumes of nickel and cobalt, industry data showed on Thursday.

The Ministry of Mines and Strategic Resources said nickel output rose 4.5% year-on-year to 18,200 metric tons, while cobalt production reached 2,800 metric tons, up 6.1% from the same period in 2023. The figures were released as part of the government’s quarterly sector review.

“This growth reflects ongoing expansion at key mining sites and continued strong demand from the global battery and electronics sectors,” said Minister of Mines Roland Raharivelo at a press conference in Antananarivo.

Madagascar’s mining sector is dominated by large-scale operations, with Sumitra Resources and Island Minerals among the major producers. Both companies reported record output for the quarter, citing favorable weather conditions and stable labor relations.

“Stable operations and a supportive regulatory environment have allowed us to optimize production,” said Marie Ravelosaona, chief executive of Island Minerals. “We remain committed to sustainable practices and local community engagement.”

Industry analysts noted that rising international prices for nickel and cobalt have benefited exporters, although logistical challenges and infrastructure constraints continue to pose risks.

“Madagascar’s metals sector is well positioned to capitalize on the ongoing boom in electric vehicle manufacturing globally,” said Rija Andrianarisoa, analyst at Malagasy Commodities Research. “However, further investment in rail and port facilities will be key to unlocking future growth.”

Gold production also edged higher, rising 2.7% to 1.65 metric tons for the quarter. The Chamber of Mines said artisanal gold mining remained a significant contributor to rural employment.

The Ministry said mining accounted for 7.3% of Madagascar’s GDP in the first quarter, and the government reaffirmed its commitment to attracting new investment through regulatory reforms and tax incentives.

No major disruptions or supply chain issues were reported during the period.
